Suggest why this is difficult to do for these experiments.

Suggest why the aqueous potassium iodate is warmed before the aqueous sodium metabisulfite
is added rather than after it has been added.

rather than leaving it in the beaker.

text: You are going to investigate the rate of the reaction between sodium metabisulfite and
potassium iodate at different temperatures.
Read all of the instructions carefully before starting the experiments.
Instructions
You are going to do five experiments at different temperatures. In each experiment the total volume
of liquid is 80cm .

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Carefully add the dilute hydrochloric acid for Question 2 to the boiling tube containing solid N.
Test any gas produced.
Keep the contents of the boiling tube for use in (b).
Record your observations.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Filter the mixture formed in the boiling tube in (a) into a test-tube until you have about 2cm
depth of filtrate in the test-tube. The filtrate collected is solution P. Divide solution P into two
approximately equal portions in two test-tubes.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
To the first portion of solution P, add aqueous sodium hydroxide gradually until it is in
excess.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
To the second portion of solution P, add aqueous ammonia gradually until it is in excess.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Identify solid N.

tests on solution O

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Carry out a flame test on solution O.
Record your observations.

Divide the remaining solution O into three approximately equal portions in three test-tubes.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Test the pH of the first portion of solution O.
pH = ______

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
To the second portion of solution O add about 1cm depth of dilute nitric acid followed by a few
drops of barium nitrate solution.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (g)
parts.text:
To the third portion of solution O add aqueous copper(II) sulfate gradually until it is in excess.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (h)
parts.text: Identify solution O.

text: You are provided with two substances, solid N and solution O.
Do the following tests on the substances, recording all of your observations at each stage.
tests on solid N
Many fizzy drinks contain phosphoric acid. Phosphoric acid reacts with sodium hydrogencarbonate
to make carbon dioxide gas.
Value Coke and Kola Koola are two fizzy drinks which contain phosphoric acid as the only acid.
Plan an investigation to find which of these two fizzy drinks contains the highest concentration of
phosphoric acid.
Include in your answer how your results will tell you which drink contains the highest concentration
of phosphoric acid.
You are provided with samples of both fizzy drinks, solid sodium hydrogencarbonate and common
laboratory apparatus.
